deep.reconstruction:
Physical context: a pencil draft written over a printed postal ledger form ('No 10. | No | Auslage | Porto | Franko'). The page has no computation in the strict sense. It is a heavily revised prose draft of the foundational lemmas Riemann placed at the start of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (J. reine angew. Math. 54, 1857): integrals of total differentials on multiply connected surfaces, and unique continuation of functions of x+yi. The previous page uses exactly these facts: log theta jumps by constants across the cuts a_nu, b_nu and l, and the integral of log theta d(epsilon_mu) around T' is used to locate the points eta. Most of the reading below is reconstructed from fragments.

(A) Top paragraph, partly encircled in the manuscript. Let X(x,y) and Y(x,y) be continuous with dX/dy = dY/dx. Then X dx + Y dy is an exact differential and Z = int (X dx + Y dy) is defined.
- If the surface is cut by a Querschnitt (cross-cut), take Z continuous in the cut surface.
- At corresponding points on the two banks of the cut, X dx + Y dy takes the same value, since X and Y are continuous across the cut and dx, dy are the same.
- My implicit step: hence d(Z+ - Z-) = 0 along the cut.
- So the difference Z+ - Z- is constant ('constant', added in the right margin). It does not change along a cross-cut, or more generally along a boundary curve. This difference is the period, or modulus of periodicity, of Z for that cut.

(B) Middle paragraph, under a struck-out heading (illegible, possibly 'Fortsetzung'). It most likely reads: 'It was proved at the outset that a function of x+yi which is given along a finite line can be continued continuously from there in only one way, and is thus completely determined.'
- Then a generalisation is attempted. Take a surface piece in which the quantities concerned are functions of x, y. If the value of (the integral of) X dx + Y dy is given on a finite line, it can be continued continuously in only one way.
- The line itself may be chosen arbitrarily. If a function vanished on both sides of a finite part of the line, it would vanish on the whole piece.
- Several attempts at stating the needed conditions (e.g. 'Bedingungen ... welche ...', 'Verlauf') are struck through. In modern terms this is the identity theorem / uniqueness of analytic continuation from a set with an accumulation point, here a curve segment.

(C) Lower fragments. These concern the integral of the complete differential X dx + Y dy, taken from a fixed initial point through the interior of a closed region.
- Its value z depends on the position of the endpoint and is treated as a function of x, y. This is perhaps viewed as a surface in x, y, z coordinates.
- The subject is how this value depends on the endpoint and changes across cuts. The text breaks off.

Role: supplies the general principle behind the jump statements for log theta on the preceding page, and the cut-system topology on the next page (curves a_1 ... a_n, Querschnitte, 'zerfällt').
errors: No mathematical errors can be identified in the legible parts. Statement (A), that the jump of an integral of a closed form across a cut is constant, is correct provided X and Y are continuous across the cut. The uniqueness statement in (B) is correct for analytic functions of x+yi. For a general closed form it needs extra hypotheses, which is plausibly why the conditions were repeatedly rewritten and struck out.

results.what: The difference of the boundary values of Z = int(X dx + Y dy), with dX/dy = dY/dx, on the two banks of a cross-cut is constant along the cut.
results.modern_name: Periods of closed 1-forms; constant jump across cuts (de Rham periods)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (1851 dissertation; 1857 Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen)

results.what: A function of x+yi given on a finite line segment can be continued continuously in only one way.
results.modern_name: Identity theorem / uniqueness of analytic continuation

results.what: The integral of an exact differential from a fixed initial point, regarded as a function z of the endpoint (x, y).
results.modern_name: Primitive of a closed form on a cut (simply connected) surface

deep.surprise_reason: This is a preparatory draft of foundational lemmas that Riemann published in 1857 ('Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen', introductory sections on functions of x+yi and Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs). It has historical interest as working material written on scrap ledger paper, but contains nothing not already known as his.

checkable.asserts: Example closed form (d arg): the integrability condition dX/dy = dY/dx holds, so it equals 0.
The jump (period) of Z across a cut from the origin equals the loop integral, 2*pi, independent of where the cut is crossed.
Functions of x+yi satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations, the setting of the uniqueness-of-continuation statement; result is 0.

transcription_corrections: The header 'No 10. | No | Auslage | Porto | Franko' is the printed postal-ledger form the draft is written on, not Riemann's text. '157' is the folio number.
Line 2 likely reads '... auf beiden Seiten gleich, da X dx+Y dy auf beiden Seiten denselben Werth annimmt'.

'constant' stands as a marginal addition at the right edge of line 3. The end of the paragraph likely reads '... längs eines Querschnitts oder allgemein einer Grenzcurve nicht ändert' rather than 'einen Querschnitt ... ändert'.

The middle paragraph probably begins 'Im Eingange ist bewiesen, dass eine Function von x+yi, die in einer endlichen Linie gegeben ist, sich nur auf eine Weise von dort aus stetig fortsetzen lässt'. The image shows 'x+yi' ('x+y i'), not 'X dx+Y dy', in this line; 'nur auf eine Weise' is to be preferred to 'einen Werth'.
'in welchem die ... x,y sind' probably reads '... Functionen von x, y sind'.
The heading above the middle paragraph is struck through. It is illegible, possibly 'Fortsetzung'.
The bottom line reads '... in Bezug auf diese ... Coordinaten x, y, z' (uncertain).
